# Digital Arts OER

HAXcms is a file-based CMS: authored pages and metadata are stored as portable files, not locked into a database-only workflow.
The canonical site structure is `site.json`, represented in JSON Outline Schema (`id`, `parent`, `order`, `slug`, `location`, and `metadata`).
Use HAX CLI and ecosystem tooling to maintain human-authored content while keeping machine-readable outputs synchronized.
Managed files (feeds, search indexes, manifests, and this `llms.txt`) are generated artifacts and should be rebuilt by tooling.

## Core resources
- [site.json](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/site.json): Canonical site manifest and navigation tree in JSON Outline Schema format.
- [llms.txt](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/llms.txt): LLM-oriented guide to this site and its machine-readable resources.

- [Project 1 launch: Sheet to form](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-86df4055-aee6-4e3c-aa9c-5e291791c8ef/index.md): Project 1 brief; theme introduction; precedents; sketching and prototyping in chipboard; the crit protocol.
- [Project 1 production + crit](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-b2b1aa00-e58f-483e-8649-84526b67110a/index.md): Production; troubleshooting cut files; finishing laser-cut work; documentation basics; Project 1 crit.
- [Additive: 3D printing fundamentals](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-dea7e7e2-d0fe-4423-ad9f-8004351ff58a/index.md): How FDM works; slicing; orientation, supports, overhangs, wall thickness, infill; materials (PLA/PETG); mesh hygiene (manifold, normals, STL/3MF); the print queue.
- [Modeling for fabrication: parametric and sculptural](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-2d373830-ce82-4cb9-a217-5d6ba17e8a6a/index.md): Two modeling attitudes: parametric CAD (Fusion 360) and mesh/sculptural (Blender); parameters, constraints, families of objects; scanning as input (photogrammetry).
- [Project 2 launch: Multiples and variation](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-23bfc330-baae-4c57-b782-7da696b33431/index.md): Project 2 brief; series, editions, variation; precedents; mid-term review of process documentation.

- [The Craftsman — Prologue: Man as His Own Maker](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-2ffcd551-9b63-4336-835e-7dd0155cb5cf/index.md): Recommended: craft as the desire to do a job well for its own sake; useful vocabulary for crit.
- [Digital Fabrications: Architectural and Material Techniques — Introduction; Sectioning; Folding](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-c9e4c050-9edb-485b-8ee3-5a5b0a659965/index.md): Organizes digital fabrication by technique family (sectioning, tessellating, folding, contouring, forming) with built examples — the vocabulary for sheet-to-form.
- [Design for 3D printing — knowledge base](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-b3c6e211-2a6d-4c98-8d00-f3159e7d4919/index.md): Practical FDM design rules (wall thickness, overhangs, tolerances); the reference for and the checklist.
- [Prusa Knowledge Base — print quality troubleshooting and slicing basics](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-3475b882-a15e-43ce-b226-750a59efa486/index.md): Recommended: diagnosing failed prints; replace with the shop's own slicer documentation once known.
- [The Alphabet and the Algorithm — ch. 1, Variable, Identical, Differential](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-a736e35a-581d-40fb-8d77-eb137a06c7e7/index.md): The theory of the digital multiple: identical copies vs. variable families; the intellectual core of Project 2.
- [Form+Code in Design, Art, and Architecture — Parameterize](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-dfb75ec5-a7d2-4bb4-a368-66f3b078a70c/index.md): Recommended: parametric thinking with art/design examples; a bridge from the program's code-based work to fabrication.
- [Digital Handmade: Craftsmanship and the New Industrial Revolution](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-5898b795-f4da-441d-aa3b-929668d03a7d/index.md): Recommended precedent source: makers and studios combining digital fabrication with craft; good for finding Project 2 examples.
- [Critical Making: Conceptual and Material Studies in Technology and Social Life](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-5d3296eb-cb97-4ccc-8bf2-e6ccedf22d62/index.md): Defines critical making — making as a way of thinking critically about technology; frames the final project.
- [Making It: Pick up a spot welder and join the revolution](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-37be7178-7d0e-47aa-9515-852942e1101f/index.md): The sharpest popular critique of the maker movement; discussed against Gershenfeld and Anderson.
- [Makers: The New Industrial Revolution — ch. 1](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-de3020be-052d-4ec8-a11d-414dc295423b/index.md): Recommended as the foil for: the boosterish version of the maker thesis.
- [Materials against materiality](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-526d73e9-2873-4210-b492-2888ab24f533/index.md): Recommended: attention to materials as processes rather than properties; useful for the finishing and hybrid-process week.
- [Thinking Through Craft — Introduction](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-24c20753-b4ef-41f4-acd4-60df13259c87/index.md): Recommended: craft as a set of positions (supplemental, material, skilled, pastoral, amateur) rather than a category of objects.
- [Shaping Things](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-0a2a466e-a69a-45e3-b4b6-53c7493455b5/index.md): Recommended: spimes — objects that carry their data and history; relevant to file-as-publication and the theme.
- [Fab Academy — How to Make (Almost) Anything class archive](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-d987aef1-4873-4380-86a5-4a902fea309d/index.md): Reference: the global fab-lab curriculum with weekly process pages; a source for demos and a model for documentation.
- [Nervous System — studio project pages](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-4208204c-37a2-4060-adb2-c094b8de1cc3/index.md): Reference precedent for generative multiples across printing, cutting, and casting. Also cited on slide 9 (Kinematics Dress, 2014) as the course's first additive example — students meet the studio on day one and return to it in.
- [The 3D Additivist Manifesto](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-60e4b429-b224-4257-bf91-839210d305a3/index.md): Short, open, 3D-printing-specific, and deliberately provocative — the counterweight to the design-guide readings in the print week; returns in as a critical-making text. Assigned at UNT.

- [Project 1: Sheet to form](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-59547add-790e-4255-a3f0-962065b0064f/index.md): Make a three-dimensional object from flat sheet material using sectioning, folding, or joinery, responding to the theme.
- [Project 2: Multiples and variation](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-e8448268-7180-455f-ba52-360dd73d16f6/index.md): Produce a series of at least five objects in which variation is designed — parametric, generative, or rule-based — and the series says something the single object cannot.
- [Final project](https://localhost:3000/learning-materials/pages/item-c64e34a7-5763-4e28-b1e2-e9b87814daf8/index.md): A self-directed project answering one of the selected themes, using at least two fabrication processes, developed through the proposal, a work-in-progress crit, and a final exhibition.
